label: External spur gear pair ratio model
adaptation_note: Pitch-ratio circles, complete unwrapped tooth counts and opposed direction glyphs. This is a quantitative teaching companion, not a replacement full meshing contour model.
acceptance_requirement: Account for 18 and 36 teeth and compatible pitch where meshing is claimed. Fewer drawn teeth cannot stand for the full ratio without explicit abstraction.

frames.title: Pitch-size relationship companion
frames.teaching_key: Two separate pitch-circle references: the small gear has 18 teeth, the large gear 36, giving a 2:1 diameter/tooth-count ratio for common pitch. Circle radii here are exactly 7 and 14 pins. They are separated for this explanation, not positioned as a meshing pair. The following count strips supply all teeth and the final frame supplies opposite rotation. No involute profile, contact or manufacturability approval is claimed.

frames.title: Small gear teeth 1–6
frames.teaching_key: Unwrapped count strip for the small gear: teeth 1 through 6 of 18. Each raised rectangular projection is one count cue. Join count ranges in order, without counting the shared strip ends as teeth. This does not claim these rectangular shapes are the source tooth profile, a meshing rack or a manufactured gear.

frames.title: Opposite rotation directions
frames.teaching_key: Equal-size direction glyphs are not pitch circles: left represents the small gear rotating clockwise, right the large gear counterclockwise. With 18 and 36 teeth and ideal external meshing, the small gear makes two turns for each one large-gear turn. Arrow size/angle does not encode that speed ratio. This direction companion does not draw the actual contact geometry.
